question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 02 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The increase in p95 latency is due to a reduction in the database pool size, leading to connection exhaustion.
why_chain: The config_change (E5) reduced the db.pool_size from 50 to 5.
This reduction in pool size caused the connection pool to become exhausted more quickly.
The increased latency and error rate (E2, E4, E6, E7, E8, E9) are symptoms of the connection pool exhaustion.

contributing_factors.description: The increase in p95 latency is also due to the increase in request volume, which put more pressure on the system.
why_chain: The request volume for service checkout increased by 24% (E3).
The increased request volume put more pressure on the system, exacerbating the connection pool exhaustion.
The connection pool exhaustion (E6, E7, E8, E9) caused the p95 latency to rise.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency is due to a change in the service configuration.
ruled_out.reason: The config_change (E5) was the only change made to the system before the p95 latency increase, and the increase in p95 latency is not a direct result of the config_change.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency is due to a change in the service's external dependencies.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence that the service's external dependencies changed or failed around the time of the p95 latency increase.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency is due to a change in the service's infrastructure.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence that the service's infrastructure changed or failed around the time of the p95 latency increase.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for service checkout rose from 222 ms to 579 ms (+161%), with a change point at 2026-03-02T10:50:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service checkout: 3 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.01).
At the same time, request volume for service checkout stayed about the same (817 per 5 min before, 1013 per 5 min after, +24%).
At the same time, error rate for service checkout rose (0.36% before, 0.53% after, +49%).
Changed checkout db.pool_size from 50 to 5 (all regions) (checkout; 1 min before the change; record R014)
checkout: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (checkout, ap-south; 2 min after the change; record R015)
p95 latency above SLO on checkout (checkout; 15 min after the change; record R018)
checkout: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (checkout, eu-west; 8 min after the change; record R016)
checkout: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (checkout, us-east; 14 min after the change; record R017)

reasons: ✓ A change event (config_changes) lines up in time (1 min before the change).
✓ 4 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Increase the db.pool_size back to 50 to prevent connection pool exhaustion.
Monitor request volume and adjust capacity if necessary to prevent connection pool exhaustion.
